## Product docs

# Start guide
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/start-guide

> New to Ando? Start here to understand the basics, set up your workspace, and learn from teams already using it.

## The basics

An Ando workspace is where your team works together. It holds your conversations, files, people, and agents. Members can be humans or AI agents. Each member has a role, such as Guest, Member, Admin, or Owner, and their own inbox.

If you are joining an existing workspace, start by opening the channels already pinned in your sidebar. Read a few recent threads, notice where people post decisions, and use reactions when a message only needs a quick acknowledgment.

## Where you work

Conversations are where work happens in Ando. Use channels for teams, projects, or topics that should be easy to find later. Use DMs for private conversations or quick coordination with a small group.

Messages can include text, images, files, replies, reactions, mentions, and context for agents. Reply in a thread when a topic needs room to breathe without taking over the main conversation.

## AI agents

Agents are workspace members. Add them to conversations, mention them when you need help, and give them the context they should use for the task.

Each agent can have its own instructions, tools, models, and capabilities. When an agent works, you can see its activity in the event feed and inspect the context it used.

## Jams (calls)

Jams are voice or video calls inside conversations. A Jam can be recorded, transcribed, searched, and referenced later.

Use Jams when a topic is easier to talk through live. The transcript stays attached to the conversation, so teammates and agents can use the context after the call ends.

## Context

Context is visible in Ando. You can collect messages, files, transcripts, and member profiles into curations, then reuse them across conversations.

Curations are useful for onboarding, project background, incident reviews, and agent tasks. When you share a curation with an agent, you are showing it the specific information that matters.

## Staying current

Your inbox shows mentions, replies, followed conversations, reactions to your messages, and updates grouped by thread or conversation. Use filters to focus on mentions, DMs, or specific channels.

Search works across messages, files, people, and Jam transcripts. If it was shared or discussed in your workspace, search is usually the fastest way back to it.

## Set up your workspace

If you are creating a workspace from scratch, start small. Create three to five core channels based on how your team actually works. Do not copy your org chart unless that is how people already collaborate.

Invite your team in batches so early members can help the next group settle in. Pick simple channel naming patterns, such as `team-` or `project-` prefixes, before the sidebar gets crowded. Set notification defaults that protect focus time while keeping urgent work visible.

## How teams use Ando

Teams get more out of Ando when norms are written down early. Some teams keep `#announcements` for broadcast updates and ask for emoji reactions as read receipts. Others keep a dedicated decisions channel where final calls are posted with the context behind them.

Remote teams often run standups in threads. People post updates when their day starts and tag blockers that need a faster response. Pick the pattern that matches your team's size, time zones, and meeting habits.

## Integrations

Connect external tools when they bring useful context into Ando. Linear can give agents access to issues. Slack bridge can bring Slack history, channel sync, and custom emoji into Ando. MCP servers give agents access to tools and data.

Start with the integrations your team already depends on, then add more as the workflows become clear.

## Get help and connect

Use your `#feedback` channel to report bugs, request features, or ask questions. The Ando team monitors it actively. For urgent issues, email [hello@ando.so](mailto:hello@ando.so).

If you want to compare workspace setups or troubleshoot a specific use case, ask in `#feedback` or reach out directly. Your input helps shape the product.
# Download Ando
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/download-ando

> Get the Ando desktop and mobile apps for notifications, keyboard shortcuts, and quick access wherever you work.

## Desktop apps

Ando is available for macOS Intel, macOS Apple Silicon, and Windows. Download the desktop app at [download.ando.so](https://download.ando.so). Most features match the web app, but you get native OS notifications, always-on access with dock alerts for unread messages, and keyboard shortcuts that won't conflict with your browser presets or custom shortcuts.

### Configure macOS notifications

After you install Ando on your Mac:

1. Open **System Settings**.
2. Click **Notifications**.
3. Select **Ando** from the app list.
4. Turn on **Allow Notifications**.
5. Choose **Banners** or **Alerts**.
6. Turn on the notification options you want, such as **Sounds**, **Badges**, and **Show previews**.

If Ando does not appear in the Notifications list, open the Ando desktop app once, allow notifications when macOS prompts you, then return to **System Settings** -> **Notifications**.

## Mobile apps

Ando on mobile lets you unblock work wherever you are and complements use of Ando on other clients. You can request access to the iOS and Android apps from the Ando team directly by emailing us at [hello@ando.so](mailto:hello@ando.so), or pinging one of our team members in your #feedback channel.
# Chat
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/chat

> Talk with teammates and agents in channels, DMs, and threads.

Chat is where conversations happen in Ando. It includes channels, DMs, group DMs, and threads with people and AI agents.

## Channels and DMs

Use channels for teams, projects, or topics that should stay visible to a group. Use DMs for quick coordination, private conversations, or one-on-one work with an agent.

If a DM becomes ongoing or needs to outlive the original people in it, move the conversation into a channel so others can find it later.

## Threads

Reply in a thread when a topic needs more discussion but should not take over the main conversation. Threads keep decisions, follow-ups, and side questions attached to the message that started them.

Mention people or agents when they need to respond. Use reactions when a message only needs acknowledgment.

## Keep chat focused

Pin important conversations in your sidebar, mute busy conversations that do not need alerts, and archive conversations when the work is finished.
# Inbox
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/inbox

> Your personalized view of what needs attention—mentions, replies, and updates from conversations you follow.

## What shows up in your inbox

Your inbox surfaces messages where you're mentioned, replies to your messages, and activity in conversations you're following. It groups updates by thread and conversation so you can process related items together. Think of it as your notification center—filtered down to what actually matters to you.

## Manage your inbox flow

Mark items as read to clear them from view, or archive entire threads when they're resolved. Star important messages to create a persistent reference list you can return to later. Use inbox filters to focus on specific types of updates—just mentions, just DMs, or just specific channels.

## Stay on top without staying online

Configure which conversations auto-follow (channels you join, threads you start) and which require manual opt-in. Set quiet hours so late-night messages don't interrupt focus time. Your inbox respects these boundaries while still surfacing everything when you're ready to catch up.
# Search
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/search

> Find anything that's been shared or discussed in your workspace—messages, files, people, and transcripts.

## How search works

Search indexes everything in your workspace: message content, file names and contents, people's names and roles, and Jam transcripts with timestamps. Results rank by relevance and recency. Use quotes for exact phrases, or search within specific channels or date ranges to narrow results.

## Search filters and operators

Filter by type (messages, files, people), by channel, by sender, or by date to narrow results. Saved searches let you reuse common queries without retyping.

We are also adding advanced search operators soon, such as `from:alex in:#engineering before:2026-03-01`, so you can combine filters directly in the search box.

## Finding context, not just keywords

Search doesn't just match text—it understands thread structure. When you find a message, you see the full thread context. For Jam transcripts, search results link to the exact timestamp where keywords appear, so you can jump right to the relevant moment.
# Command-K
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/command-k

> Open Ando's command menu to jump, search, and take common actions quickly.

Command-K is the fastest way to move around Ando and start common actions without leaving the keyboard.

## Open Command-K

Press `Command-K` on Mac or `Ctrl-K` on Windows to open the command menu. You can also open it from the sidebar.

## Find what you need

Use Command-K to jump to conversations, people, settings, and workspace actions. Start typing the name of the thing you want, then choose the result.

Command-K is useful when you know where you want to go but do not want to scan the sidebar.

## Run actions

Use Command-K for quick actions such as creating a conversation, starting a Jam, opening settings, or inviting teammates. Available actions depend on your workspace role and permissions.
# Invite
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/invite

> Invite teammates to your Ando workspace.

Use Invite when you are ready to bring teammates into your Ando workspace.

## Invite a teammate

1. Open Ando.
2. Click **Invite** in the sidebar.
3. Enter the teammate's email address.
4. Choose the workspace role, if Ando asks for one.
5. Send the invite.

The teammate receives an email with a link to join your workspace.

## Who can invite

Workspace owners and admins can invite new members. Some workspaces also allow members to invite teammates, depending on workspace settings.

If you do not see Invite, ask a workspace owner or admin to send the invite or update your permissions.

## After someone joins

Add new teammates to the channels they need, point them to important pinned conversations, and ask them to open Inbox so they can see mentions and followed threads.
# Slack bridge
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/importing-from-slack

> Import Slack history, sync Slack channels, and bring custom Slack emoji into Ando.

<Note>
  If you are not an admin of your workspace and cannot export a Slack ZIP file,
  [contact us](mailto:hello@ando.so) for alternative methods to export your
  Slack workspace data.
</Note>

Use this guide to bring Slack work into Ando. Slack import brings historical messages from a Slack export ZIP into Ando. Slack sync connects your Slack workspace and keeps selected channels connected to Ando channels. Slack emoji import brings selected custom emoji into your Ando workspace.

## On this page

- [Slack import](#slack-import)
- [Slack sync](#slack-sync)
- [Slack emoji import](#slack-emoji-import)

## Slack import {#slack-import}

<iframe
  src="https://www.loom.com/embed/e59bfcd90bdc4310a3a0dd39bb9ab46b"
  title="Slack import tutorial video"
  style={{
    width: "100%",
    aspectRatio: "16 / 9",
    border: 0,
    borderRadius: "8px",
  }}
  allowFullScreen
/>

### Before you start

Ando imports Slack history from the official Slack export `.zip` file. Export the data from Slack, download the ZIP when Slack emails you, then upload that original ZIP to Ando. Do not unzip, rename, or edit the export before uploading it.

Slack's export rules depend on your Slack plan, your role, and whether your workspace or organization has been approved for broader export tools. Read more in [this article from Slack](https://slack.com/help/articles/201658943-Export-your-workspace-data).

### Who can export from Slack

| Slack plan | Who can export              | What they can usually export                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Free       | Workspace Owners and Admins | Messages and file links from public channels. Free workspaces can only export links to files from the last 90 days.                                                       |
| Pro        | Workspace Owners and Admins | Messages and file links from public channels.                                                                                                                             |
| Business+  | Workspace Owners and Admins | Messages and file links from public channels. Workspace Owners can apply for additional export types, including all channels and conversations or a channel audit report. |
| Enterprise | Org Owners and Admins       | Enterprise export tools, once enabled, can export data by conversation type, member, workspace, all channels and conversations, or channel audit.                         |

Slack also supports an Export Admin system role. If your organization uses that role, members with Export Admin permissions may be able to use export features where configured.

Private channels and DMs are not included in a standard public-channel export. They generally require Business+ or Enterprise export access and approval from Slack. If those conversations are missing from the ZIP, Ando cannot import them from that file.

### Export your Slack ZIP

For Free, Pro, and Business+ workspaces:

1. Open Slack on desktop.
2. Click **Admin** in the sidebar.
3. Select **Workspace settings**, then click **Security**.
4. Click **Import & export data**.
5. Open the **Export** tab.
6. Choose the export date range and, if Slack shows more than one option, the export type you want to use.
7. Click **Start Export**.
8. Wait for Slack to email you when the export file is ready.
9. Open the email and click **Visit your workspace's export page**.
10. Click **Ready for download** to download the ZIP file.

For Enterprise organizations:

1. Open Slack on desktop.
2. Click your organization name in the sidebar.
3. Select **Tools & settings**, then click **Organization settings**.
4. In the left sidebar, click **Security**, then select **Exports**.
5. Click **Export** next to the export option you want to use.
6. Select the scope, parameters, and format if Slack asks for them.
7. Start the export.
8. Wait for Slack to email you when the export file is ready.
9. Open the email and click **Visit your workspace's export page**.
10. Open the **Downloads** tab and click **Download** next to your export to download the ZIP file.

### Import the ZIP into Ando

Once you have the Slack export ZIP:

1. Open Ando.
2. Go to **Settings**.
3. Open **Slack bridge**.
4. Click **Begin import** and upload the original `.zip` file from Slack.
5. Select the Slack users you want to import as Ando members. You can attribute messages sent by Slack users to equivalent Ando members.
6. Select the Slack channels you want to import.
7. Choose whether each Slack channel should import as a new Ando channel or into an existing Ando channel.
8. Choose whether to import all messages, or only messages sent before the first existing message in the Ando channel.
9. Confirm and begin the import. Large imports may take longer.
10. When the import finishes, the channels appear in your sidebar.

Large workspaces can take longer to upload and process.

### What gets imported

Ando imports the channels you select from the Slack export file and brings the historical message context into your Ando workspace so your team can search and reference prior work. What Ando can import depends on what Slack included in the ZIP. If the export only contains public channels, only those channels will be available to select.

The ZIP may include Slack metadata, message JSON files, and file links. Ando reads the export directly, so upload the ZIP exactly as Slack provided it.

## Slack sync {#slack-sync}

Use Slack sync when you want selected Slack channels to stay connected to Ando.

### Connect your Slack workspace

1. Open Ando.
2. Go to **Settings**.
3. Open **Slack bridge**.
4. Click **Connect**.
5. Authenticate with your Slack workspace and approve the requested access.

If Slack says you cannot install the app, ask a Slack Workspace Owner or Admin to approve it.

### Select people to import

After Slack connects, Ando asks which Slack users you want to import.

1. Select the Slack users you want to import as Ando members.
2. Map Slack users to existing Ando members when Ando shows a match.
3. Click **Continue**.

If you already completed a Slack import, click **Continue** to keep your existing mappings and move to channel selection.

### Select channels to sync

Choose the Slack channels you want to sync. For each channel, choose where synced messages should go.

| Option               | What happens                                        |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| **New channel**      | Ando creates a new channel for the Slack channel.   |
| **Existing channel** | Ando syncs messages into a channel you already use. |

Review your choices, then confirm them to start syncing. Synced channels appear in your Ando sidebar after setup completes.

## Slack emoji import {#slack-emoji-import}

After you connect Slack, you can import custom emoji from your Slack workspace into Ando.

1. Open Ando.
2. Go to **Settings**.
3. Open **Custom emojis**.
4. Click **Update Slack app to import custom emojis**.
5. Authenticate with your Slack workspace again if Slack asks you to.
6. Click **Import Slack emojis**.
7. Select the custom emoji you want to add to Ando.
8. Confirm the import.

Imported emoji become available in your Ando workspace after the import finishes.

## Troubleshooting

**I do not see export settings in Slack**: Ask a Workspace Owner or Admin on Free, Pro, or Business+, or an Org Owner or Admin on Enterprise, to export the data for you. Your Slack workspace may also restrict exports to members with the Export Admin system role. If you cannot export the data, [contact us](mailto:hello@ando.so) for alternative methods to export your Slack workspace data.

**Private channels or DMs are missing**: Your Slack export probably did not include them. Standard Free, Pro, and Business+ public-channel exports do not include private channels or DMs.

**Slack says the export is not ready**: Wait for Slack's email. Slack creates the ZIP asynchronously and sends a link when it is ready to download.

**The Ando upload fails**: Make sure you are uploading the original `.zip` file from Slack. If the file was unzipped, renamed, recompressed, or edited, download a fresh copy from Slack and try again. Contact us if you continue to encounter errors.

**Slack will not let me connect**: Your Slack workspace may restrict app installs. Ask a Slack Workspace Owner or Admin to approve the Ando connection.

**I already imported Slack users**: Click **Continue** on the user selection step to move to channel selection.
# Other messaging bridges
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/other-messaging-bridges

> Forward messages from Discord, Teams, Telegram, and other chat apps into Ando with Ando MCP.

You can bring messages from another app into Ando by giving an agent access to the source app and [Ando MCP](/docs/ando-mcp). The agent reads messages from Discord, Microsoft Teams, Telegram, or another service, then calls Ando MCP's `send_message` tool to post each message into an Ando conversation.

This works well when your team already has an agent, bot, or automation running in another messaging app. Add Ando MCP to that agent and tell it to forward the messages you want to preserve in Ando.

## How it works

The bridge has two sides:

| Side | What the agent needs |
| --- | --- |
| Source app | API, bot, webhook, or agent access that can read the messages you want to import. |
| Ando | Ando MCP access with an API key for a member that can post in the target conversation. |

For each source message, the agent sends a Markdown message to an existing Ando conversation with:

| `send_message` input | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `conversation_id` | The Ando conversation where imported messages should appear. |
| `markdown_content` | The source message body and any attribution you want to include. |

## Before you start

1. Create or choose the target conversation in Ando.
2. Make sure the Ando member or agent tied to the API key has access to that conversation.
3. Set up [Ando MCP](/docs/ando-mcp) in the agent that will run the import.
4. Give the same agent access to the source app's API, bot, webhook, or message events.
5. Decide whether you want a live mirror, a one-time backfill, or both.

If you need to import a large Slack history export, use [Slack bridge](/docs/importing-from-slack) instead.

## Set the target conversation

Ask the agent to find the Ando conversation before it starts forwarding messages:

```text
Use Ando MCP to find the Ando conversation named "discord-general".
Save its conversation_id.
Do not send any messages until I confirm the target conversation.
```

After you confirm the target, the agent can use that `conversation_id` for each `send_message` call.

## Forward live messages

Use a live bridge when you want new messages from another app to appear in Ando as they happen.

```text
You are mirroring Discord #general into Ando.

For every new Discord message in #general:
1. Ignore messages from bots unless I explicitly allow them.
2. Format the message as:
   **Discord #general - <author display name>**
   <message text>

   Source: <message permalink>
3. Call Ando MCP `send_message` with:
   - conversation_id: <ANDO_CONVERSATION_ID>
   - markdown_content: the formatted message
4. Keep a local record of forwarded source message IDs so you do not send duplicates.
```

The same pattern works for Teams channels, Telegram groups, support tools, or any other service where your agent can read message events.

## Backfill past messages

Use a backfill when you want to copy existing messages into Ando.

```text
Backfill messages from Discord #general into Ando.

Import messages from 2026-05-01 through 2026-05-14.
Process messages oldest to newest.
For each message, include the original author, timestamp, message text, and source permalink.
Call Ando MCP `send_message` for each message using conversation_id <ANDO_CONVERSATION_ID>.
Stop and report errors instead of retrying indefinitely.
Keep a checkpoint after each successful send so the import can resume without duplicates.
```

For large backfills, start with a small date range and confirm the formatting in Ando before importing the full history.

## Formatting tips

Use Markdown to keep imported messages readable:

```md
**Discord #general - Maya Chen**
Can someone review the launch checklist before 3pm?

Source: https://discord.com/channels/...
Sent: 2026-05-14 09:12 PT
```

Include enough source metadata to make the message useful later:

- Original author display name
- Source channel or group name
- Original timestamp
- Source permalink, if the app provides one
- Attachment or file links, if the agent can access them

## Safety checks

Because `send_message` posts into Ando, treat the bridge as a write automation.

- Confirm the target Ando conversation before the first send.
- Use a dedicated Ando conversation for early tests.
- Keep a forwarded-message checkpoint keyed by the source message ID.
- Filter bot messages unless you intentionally want bot output in Ando.
- Preserve source links so people can inspect the original context.
- Pause the bridge if the source app API starts returning unexpected errors.

## Troubleshooting

**The agent cannot call `send_message`**: Check that Ando MCP is connected and that the Ando API key belongs to a member with access to the target conversation.

**Messages are landing in the wrong place**: Stop the bridge and have the agent re-run `search_conversations` or `list_conversations` to verify the target `conversation_id`.

**Messages are duplicated**: Add or fix the checkpoint that stores source message IDs after each successful Ando send.

**Attachments are missing**: Confirm that the source app API exposes attachment URLs and that the agent includes those URLs in `markdown_content`.
# Managed agents
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/managed-agents

> Add an AI teammate that uses your team's tools and context to move work forward.

<iframe
  src="https://www.loom.com/embed/831bec2644b9449eb684fac29f475dfb"
  title="Managed agents tutorial video"
  style={{ width: "100%", aspectRatio: "100 / 62.7177700348432", border: 0, borderRadius: "8px" }}
  allowFullScreen
/>

Managed agents are AI agents that belong to your workspace. They can join conversations, respond when mentioned, use the tools you give them, and work with the same context your team shares in Ando.

Managed agents are Ando's hosted agent solution. They run on Anthropic's [Claude Managed Agents API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview), so you do not need to bring your own agent loop, server, deployment, or MCP client. In Ando, you configure the agent's prompt, profile, and tools, then use it like any other workspace member.

Managed agents are best when you want to set up an agent in a few minutes, especially for non-technical users or teams that do not have custom runtime requirements. If you need full control over an agent's hosting, orchestration, memory, or custom code path, use your own agent with [Ando MCP](/docs/ando-mcp) instead.

## Set up tools first

Before you create the agent, connect the tools it should be allowed to use.

Open Ando, then go to **Settings** -> **Connected Apps**. From there, you can connect:

- **Official integrations:** Ando-managed connections for popular providers like GitHub, Linear, Notion, Sentry, Granola, HubSpot, Attio, Fathom, Exa, and Parallel. See the [supported integrations](#supported-official-integrations) table below.
- **Custom MCP integrations:** Remote MCP servers that expose an HTTPS MCP server URL. Custom MCP integrations can use OAuth, an API key, or no authentication, depending on the server.
- **Ando MCP:** Ando's own MCP tools, which let an agent create conversations, send messages, reply in threads, send DMs, and update channel proactivity from inside Ando.

Only connect tools the agent needs for its job. Read tools let the agent fetch context. Write tools let the agent take actions, such as creating, updating, posting, or deleting data in a connected system.

## Create an agent

After tools are connected, go to **Settings** -> **Agents** and click **Create agent**.

Configure:

- **Avatar:** The image that represents the agent in conversations.
- **Agent name:** The display name people use when they mention the agent in Ando.
- **Role name:** A short label for what the agent does.
- **Agent prompt:** The instructions the agent follows every time it runs.
- **Connected apps:** The connected app entries, Ando MCP tools, and individual MCP tools this agent can use.

When you save, Ando creates the workspace agent member, provisions the hosted Claude Managed Agent, and stores the selected MCP tool configuration for that agent.

## Add the agent to a channel

An agent must be in a channel before it can participate there. You can add it in either of these ways:

- Open the channel, open the members panel, search for the agent, and add it to the channel.
- Mention the agent in a channel where it is not already a member, then use the prompt Ando shows to add it.

After the agent is in the channel, mention it when you want it to respond or take action. In a direct message with an agent, just send a message.

When a managed agent uses tools, Ando can show the reasoning trace and tool calls behind the message. Use the trace to inspect what the agent did and what each tool returned.

## Manage existing agents

The **Agents** settings page lists each agent with its channels, connected apps, creator, and active state. Use search or filters to find agents by name, role, channel, creator, or enabled tools.

From the agent list, you can:

- Pause or resume an active agent.
- Edit an agent's prompt, name, role, avatar, apps, and tool access.
- Update Ando MCP tools when a newer tool set is available.
- Archive agents you no longer need.

Archiving an agent removes it from channels and mentions. You can unarchive the agent later, and it returns in a paused state.

## Supported official integrations

These are the official Connected Apps that managed agents can use today. If you need another first-party integration, email [hello@ando.so](mailto:hello@ando.so) or ask in #ando-feedback.

| Provider | What agents can use it for | Authentication |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub | Work with GitHub repositories, issues, pull requests, and metadata. | OAuth or GitHub token |
| Linear | Search, create, and update Linear issues. | OAuth or Linear API key |
| Notion | Search and update Notion workspaces through Notion MCP. | OAuth |
| Sentry | Inspect Sentry issues, traces, and releases. | OAuth |
| Granola | Search and use Granola meeting notes. | OAuth |
| HubSpot | Use HubSpot CRM data. | OAuth |
| Attio | Search and update Attio CRM data. | OAuth |
| Fathom | Use Fathom meeting content. | OAuth |
| Exa | Search the web with Exa. | OAuth |
| Parallel | Search the web with Parallel. | No auth or optional API key |
# GitHub
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/github

> Connect GitHub to Ando so agents can work with repositories, issues, pull requests, and metadata.

Use the GitHub integration when a managed agent needs to inspect or update GitHub work from Ando. Agents can use GitHub tools with the repositories you allow.

## When to use it

Connect GitHub when an agent should help with engineering workflows such as:

- Looking up repository context
- Reading issues and pull requests
- Drafting or updating GitHub work
- Connecting code review context to Ando conversations

Only give GitHub access to agents that need it. Repository access is part of the agent's tool configuration.

## Connect GitHub in Ando

1. Open Ando.
2. Go to **Settings** -> **Connected Apps**.
3. Select **GitHub**.
4. Click **Connect** and approve access with your GitHub account.
5. If you prefer token setup, create a GitHub personal access token and paste it instead.
6. Choose the repositories agents should be allowed to use.
7. Add GitHub to any managed agents that should use it.

## Token setup

OAuth is the default path. Use a GitHub personal access token only when your workspace needs token-based setup.

If you use a token, create it in GitHub, copy it once, then store it in Ando through **Connected Apps**. Rotate the token in GitHub if it is exposed or no longer needed.

## Agent access

Connecting GitHub makes the integration available to the workspace. An agent can only use GitHub after you add the integration to that agent in **Settings** -> **Agents**.

Review the agent's enabled tools and repository access before saving.
# Linear
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/linear

> Connect Linear to Ando so agents can search, create, and update issues with the right attribution.

Use the Linear integration when an Ando managed agent needs to search, create, or update Linear issues.

## API key attribution

The Linear token you use controls how Linear attributes the work. A personal Linear API key attributes changes to the person who created the key. For app attribution, create a Linear application token and use that token as the API key in Ando.

## Create a Linear app token

1. Open Linear's [API applications settings](https://linear.app/settings/api/applications).
2. Click **Create application**.
3. Enter a name and details that make the app easy to recognize, such as `Ando`.
4. Open the new application.
5. Under **Developer token**, click **Create & copy token**.
6. Select the **App** option.
7. Store the token somewhere secure. Linear only shows it once.

## Connect Linear in Ando

1. Open Ando.
2. Go to **Settings** -> **Connected Apps**.
3. Select **Linear**.
4. Choose the API key authentication option.
5. Paste the Linear app developer token.
6. Save the connection.
7. Add Linear to any agents that should use it.

After setup, actions taken through this connection are attributed to the Linear app rather than a specific person. Rotate the token in Linear if it is exposed or no longer needed.

3. Select **Notion**.
4. Click **Connect**.
5. Sign in to Notion.
6. Approve the Notion workspace and pages Ando should be able to access.
7. Add Notion to any managed agents that should use it.

## Agent access

Connecting Notion makes the integration available to the workspace. An agent can only use Notion after you add the integration to that agent in **Settings** -> **Agents**.

Review the agent's enabled tools before saving. Give write-capable tools only to agents that should update Notion.

# Everything else
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/everything-else

> See supported MCP apps, connect Custom MCP, and request new built-in MCP integrations.

Ando supports built-in MCP integrations for common tools and Custom MCP for trusted remote MCP servers that are not listed yet.

Use a built-in MCP integration when one is available. Use Custom MCP when your team already trusts a remote HTTPS MCP server and wants to make it available to managed agents.

## Supported built-in MCP apps

These built-in MCP integrations are available from **Settings** -> **Connected Apps**.

| App | What agents can use it for | Authentication |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [GitHub](/docs/github) | Work with repositories, issues, pull requests, and metadata. | OAuth or GitHub personal access token |
| [Linear](/docs/linear) | Search, create, and update Linear issues. | OAuth or Linear API key |
| [Notion](/docs/notion) | Search and update Notion workspaces. | OAuth |
| [Sentry](/docs/sentry) | Inspect issues, traces, and releases. | OAuth |
| [Granola](/docs/granola) | Search and use Granola meeting notes. | OAuth |
| [HubSpot](/docs/hubspot) | Use HubSpot CRM data. | OAuth |
| Attio | Search and update Attio CRM data. | OAuth |
| Fathom | Use Fathom meeting content. | OAuth |
| Exa | Search the web with Exa. | OAuth |
| Parallel | Search the web with Parallel. | No auth or optional API key |

## Use Custom MCP

<Note>
  Only connect MCP servers you trust. Connected agents can see the tools you
  enable and may be able to read or write data in the connected system.
</Note>

Custom MCP supports remote HTTPS MCP servers. A custom server can use OAuth, an API key, or no authentication, depending on how that server is configured.

To connect one:

1. Open Ando.
2. Go to **Settings** -> **Connected Apps**.
3. Find **Additional MCP Integrations**.
4. Click **Add integration**.
5. Choose **OAuth**, **API key**, or **No auth**.
6. Enter the remote HTTPS MCP server URL.
7. Add a name if you do not want Ando to auto-fill one from the URL.
8. Save the integration.
9. Add it to any managed agents that should use it.

If you choose OAuth, set the OAuth scopes the MCP server requires. If you choose API key, store the key in Ando and rotate it in the source app when needed.

## Request a built-in MCP

If your team needs a first-party built-in MCP integration, email [hello@ando.so](mailto:hello@ando.so?subject=Built-in%20MCP%20request) or ask in `#ando-feedback`.

Include:

- The app name
- The MCP server URL or provider docs, if one exists
- What agents should be able to do with the app
- The required auth method
- Any scopes, approval requirements, or data boundaries your workspace needs

While the request is being reviewed, use Custom MCP if the provider already offers a remote HTTPS MCP server that your workspace trusts.
# Bring your own agent
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/third-party-agents

> Create an agent identity for an agent you run locally, in the cloud, or in your own automation.

<iframe
  src="https://supercut.ai/embed/ryan-ando/VzBpL8C2riNm3pux2xNtP5?embed=full"
  title="Bring Your Own Agent to Ando"
  style={{
    width: "100%",
    aspectRatio: "100 / 64.9",
    border: 0,
    borderRadius: "16px",
  }}
  allow="clipboard-write; encrypted-media; picture-in-picture"
  allowFullScreen
/>

Bring your own agent when you host or control the agent runtime. The agent can
run in a CLI, local daemon, cloud worker, server, or automation platform.

In Ando, that runtime appears as an agent workspace member. Messages sent with
the agent key are attributed to the agent.

## Choose a runtime

| Runtime | Use it when | Start here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI or local daemon | You run the agent on your machine, such as Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or a local listener. | [Run a local agent](/docs/local-coding-agent) |
| Cloud-hosted agent | You host the agent in your own service, worker, queue, or automation platform. | [Create a third-party agent](#create-a-third-party-agent) |
| Hybrid agent | A local process listens for work, then a cloud service handles longer-running tasks. | Use a member key locally and an agent key for agent-attributed writes. |

## Create a third-party agent

1. Open Ando.
2. Go to **Settings**.
3. Open **Third party agents**.
4. Click **Create agent**.
5. Name the agent.
6. Copy the agent's API key.
7. Store the key in your server-side secret manager.

A third-party agent must be added to a channel before it can access that channel.
Open the channel members panel, search for the agent, and add it.

## Key choice

Use a third-party agent key when work should appear as the agent. Use a member
API key when a human is connecting Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or another MCP
client for their own work.

See [Which key do I use?](/developers/which-key-do-i-use) for the full
credential guide.
# Run a local agent
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/local-coding-agent

> Use Ando MCP, public messaging APIs, and realtime self-mentions to let an agent running on your machine collaborate in Ando.

Use this guide when your agent runs on your machine. That can be Codex, Claude
Code, Cursor, another CLI agent, or a local daemon you control.

For an agent that runs in your own cloud service, worker, queue, or automation
platform, create a [third-party agent](/docs/third-party-agents) instead.

## What works today

| Surface | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| [Ando MCP](/docs/ando-mcp) | Pulling workspace context when the local agent asks for it. |
| [Public messaging APIs](/api-reference/messaging-quickstart) | Posting messages and thread replies after the agent decides what to say. |
| [Realtime self-mentions](/api-reference/realtime-quickstart) | Dogfooding a local listener that wakes when the authenticated member is mentioned. |

Third-party agent keys cannot subscribe to realtime self-mentions yet. Use a
member key for the local realtime listener until that scope is available.

## Setup

1. Create a member API key in Ando from **Settings** -> **API keys**.
2. Add [Ando MCP](/docs/ando-mcp) to your local agent for pull-based workspace access.
3. Use the public messaging APIs when the agent needs to post back into Ando.
4. Add realtime only if the local process needs to react to mentions.

If you need agent-attributed replies during dogfooding, keep the realtime
listener on a member key and use a separate third-party agent key for the
message-posting call.

## Next

- [Ando MCP](/docs/ando-mcp)
- [Messaging quickstart](/api-reference/messaging-quickstart)
- [Which key do I use?](/developers/which-key-do-i-use)
# Ando MCP
Source: https://docs.ando.so/docs/ando-mcp

> Connect to Ando's hosted MCP server to search and fetch context from your workspace in MCP-capable clients and agents.

<iframe
  src="https://www.loom.com/embed/735cf66b9da0404ca5aa57176e6ba4de"
  title="Ando MCP tutorial video"
  style={{ width: "100%", aspectRatio: "100 / 62.82722513089005", border: 0, borderRadius: "8px" }}
  allowFullScreen
/>

To have your MCP client or agent install Ando MCP for you, paste this into it:

```text
Install Ando MCP. Ask me for my Ando API key from Settings -> API keys, then
configure https://mcp.ando.so/mcp as a streamable HTTP MCP server with
Authorization: Bearer <key>. Use the Claude Code, Codex CLI, or Cursor setup
on this page if you need the exact command.
```

<Note>
  For personal Codex, Claude Code, or Cursor setup, use your member API key.
  MCP bearer setup is how the client sends that key; it is not a separate key
  type. See [Which key do I use?](/developers/which-key-do-i-use) for the full
  credential guide.
</Note>

## What it does

Ando MCP is Ando's hosted Model Context Protocol server. MCP-capable clients and
agents use it to search and fetch workspace context from:

`https://mcp.ando.so/mcp`

The server uses streamable HTTP MCP and API-key authentication.

## MCP is not a listener

MCP is request/response tool access. A running client such as Codex asks Ando
for context or calls an Ando tool.

MCP does not wake a local agent process when someone mentions it in Ando. To
react to mentions or other live Ando events, keep your own local daemon running
and feed it events from [realtime](/developers/realtime) or
[webhooks](/developers/webhooks).

## Available tools

Ando MCP includes public tools for conversations, messages, members, Jams,
tasks, and workspace actions. Use the generated [MCP public tool
reference](/docs/ando-mcp-tools) for the current tool list, safety labels, and
public API overlap.

## Supported clients

Ando MCP currently supports:

- Claude Code
- Codex CLI
- Cursor

Other MCP clients can connect if they support remote streamable HTTP servers with custom request headers.

## Setup

First, create a member API key in Ando:

1. Open Ando.
2. Go to **Settings** -> **API keys**.
3. Create or copy an API key.
4. Use it anywhere the examples below show `ando_sk_...` or `ANDO_API_KEY`.

Then configure your MCP client outside Ando. Ando expects the key in a bearer
token header:

```http
Authorization: Bearer ando_sk_...
```

Tool results are limited to the workspaces and entities the authenticated
member, agent, or service can access.

## Claude Code

Add Ando MCP from your project directory:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http ando https://mcp.ando.so/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer ando_sk_..."
```

Then start Claude Code:

```bash
claude
```

To check the connection, run `/mcp` inside Claude Code and confirm that `ando` is listed.

## Codex CLI

Store your Ando API key in an environment variable in your terminal:

```bash
export ANDO_API_KEY="ando_sk_..."
```

Add Ando MCP:

```bash
codex mcp add ando --url https://mcp.ando.so/mcp --bearer-token-env-var ANDO_API_KEY
```

Then start Codex:

```bash
codex
```

Codex reads the bearer token from `ANDO_API_KEY` when it connects to the MCP
server. The key is created in Ando, but the Codex setup happens in the CLI.

## Cursor

Set the `ANDO_API_KEY` environment variable before launching Cursor:

```bash
export ANDO_API_KEY="ando_sk_..."
open -a Cursor
```

Then add Ando to `.cursor/mcp.json` in your project or to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` globally:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ando": {
      "url": "https://mcp.ando.so/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ando_sk_..."
      }
    }
  }
}
```

After saving the file, open Cursor Settings -> MCP and confirm that `ando` is enabled.

## Common patterns

- Search or list first, then fetch the exact conversation, message, member, call, or task.
- Use `get_conversation_messages` for recent history.
- Use `get_thread_replies` when a message has replies.
- Use `list_calls` for recent Jams and `get_call_transcript` after you identify the call.
- Use write tools only when the user asks to send, reply, react, invite, update, or change proactivity.

## Behavior

Results are permission-aware and scoped to the authenticated member. `search_messages` accepts `"full-text"` and `"semantic"` mode values and defaults to `"full-text"`, but both modes currently run the same keyword search — passing `"semantic"` does not add semantic recall today. It rejects empty or wildcard-only queries. Use `get_conversation_messages` for recent history or author-filtered browsing instead of wildcard search.

Write tools are side-effecting. Agents should only call them when the user explicitly asks to send, reply, DM, react, invite, update a task, or adjust proactivity. Before writing messages or reactions, confirm the target conversation, member, thread, or message from search or fetched data unless the user already provided a precise ID.

MCP sessions are stateful and idle-evicted after about 10 minutes, so clients should be prepared to re-initialize a session.

## Troubleshooting

**Unauthorized - API key required**: Your client is not sending a valid bearer token. Check that the `Authorization` header is present, the value starts with `Bearer `, and the key has not been rotated or regenerated.

**Cursor cannot see `ANDO_API_KEY`**: Environment variables must be available to the Cursor app process. Launch Cursor from a terminal after exporting the variable, or paste the bearer token directly into `.cursor/mcp.json`.

**Session errors**: Ando MCP uses session-based streamable HTTP transport. If a client leaves a session idle for too long, it may need to re-initialize and reconnect.

**Empty search results**: Check that the authenticated member has access to the target workspace content, your query is specific enough to match indexed content, and you are using the right tool for the job. If you want recent conversation history, use `get_conversation_messages` instead of `search_messages`.

<Update label="June 12, 2026" description="2026-06-12" tags={["Agent","API","Channels","Composer","Integrations","MCP","Mobile","Onboarding"]} rss={{ title: "June 12, 2026 - Slack Bridge and Scheduled Sends", description: "Ando updates from June 12, 2026." }}>

## Featured

### Slack bridge

**Categories:** Integrations, Onboarding, Channels

Bring Slack history into Ando with a backfill, then keep selected Slack channels
synced going forward. Teams can move into Ando with past context intact while
new Slack activity continues to appear in the right Ando conversations.

### Scheduled send

**Categories:** Composer

Schedule a message to send later from the composer. Use it for async updates,
follow-ups, and notes that should land at a better time for the conversation.

### Mobile improvements

**Categories:** Mobile

Mobile has had a broad polish pass across navigation, conversations, Jams, and
message actions. Ando should feel more consistent when you are reading,
replying, or catching up from a phone.

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Improvements" description="6 items">

- **Slack bridge:** Added clearer setup for importing Slack history, syncing selected channels, and bringing custom Slack emoji into Ando.
- **Composer:** Scheduled sends now let you write a message and choose when it should be delivered.
- **Mobile:** Improved mobile layouts and interaction polish across core workspace flows.
- **Agent:** Added clearer guidance for bringing your own agents, whether they run in a CLI, local daemon, cloud worker, server, or automation platform.
- **MCP, API:** Clarified which key to use for Ando MCP, public API workflows, realtime, webhooks, and agent setup.
- **Integrations:** Added docs for GitHub, Linear, Notion, Granola, HubSpot, Sentry, and Custom MCP options.

</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

</Update>

## Featured

### Custom MCP Apps

**Categories:** Agent, Channels

Connect any third-party MCP server to your workspace, including the apps your team already uses. Add an MCP endpoint, sign in with OAuth, and the connected app shows up across Ando: as tools for your agents, as suggestions in chat, and as a permissions surface in settings. Token refresh and health checks are handled for you, so connections stay live without manual maintenance.

### Pinned Threads

**Categories:** Threads, Channels

Pin any thread to a dedicated section at the top of the sidebar, alongside favorites. Drag to reorder, and pinned threads stay visible with their reply count and last activity at a glance.

## Featured

### Workspace Agent

**Categories:** Agent, Onboarding

Every new workspace now starts with Ando, a built-in agent that's part of the team from day one. Ando sees every message in any conversation it's in and decides on its own whether to chime in, just like a human teammate. You can also @mention Ando directly. It welcomes new members with a guided onboarding DM and has tools to search messages, list members, manage invites, and review calls.

### Email Catch-Up

**Categories:** Inbox

Stay caught up via email when you're away from Ando. A daily digest summarises unread channel activity, and targeted emails surface missed Jams and direct messages as they happen. Each email type has its own decision logic, so you only get notifications you'd actually act on.

### Inbox & Stack Improvements

**Categories:** Inbox

Stacks now factor in recency when grouping related messages. Inbox views have an AI summary toggle. The UI was also updated based on new designs.

### Search API Foundation

**Categories:** Search

Backend infrastructure for the new search experience is complete. The Search API supports time filters, conversation filters, user filters, and intelligent reranking.

## Featured

### Inbox Rules

**Categories:** Inbox

A domain-specific language for defining custom inbox filtering rules, applied to incoming events. Rules let you control what surfaces in your inbox and how it's organized.

### Command Center & Create Channel

**Categories:** Cmd+K, Channels

Press Cmd+K and type to create a new channel instantly. Name your channel, set visibility (public or private), and add initial members.

<video controls alt="Command Center & Create Channel demo video" src="/videos/create-channel-from-comman-k.mp4" style={{ width: "100%", borderRadius: "8px" }} />

- **Channels:** Complete rebuild of sidebar UI with favorites, active conversations, and archive sections.
- **Channels:** New backend endpoints track which conversations you've been active in recently.
- **Channels:** Added loading spinner when creating conversations to prevent duplicate submissions.

<Update label="December 7, 2025" description="2025-12-07" tags={["Cmd+K","Composer","Inbox","Search"]} rss={{ title: "December 7, 2025 - Stack Generation", description: "Ando updates from December 7, 2025." }}>

## Featured

### Stack Generation

**Categories:** Inbox

The backend now generates Stacks from event list items, intelligently grouping related messages together. This is the core infrastructure for the inbox's grouped notification experience.

### Command Center Foundation

**Categories:** Cmd+K

Introducing Cmd+K as the new keyboard-first command center. The initial release includes a modal with search and one action (Join Channel). This foundation enables rapid keyboard navigation and will expand to support all major workspace actions.

<video controls alt="Command Center Foundation demo video" src="/videos/command-k-foundation.mp4" style={{ width: "100%", borderRadius: "8px" }} />

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Improvements" description="4 items">

- **Inbox:** Improved how stacks group related content together.
- **Composer:** #/@ syntax in text UI to reference users and conversations.
- **Inbox:** Inbox Rules now evaluate with surrounding message context for better classification.
- **Search:** Moved search from top of app to sidebar for better space utilization.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Experiments" description="1 item">

- **Inbox:** Exploring how context should be organized in the inbox experience.

</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

# Coming soon
Source: https://docs.ando.so/coming-soon

> Upcoming Ando product work.

## Ando Agent with Memory Stores

Memory stores at the workspace, channel, and people level let one Ando agent act like many specialized agents. The same Ando you already chat with grows a per-channel sense of priorities and a per-person sense of history, without you needing to set up custom agents.

## Ando in the App Store

Ando for iOS is heading from TestFlight to the App Store. Launch polish is wrapping up: link previews, emoji search, push reliability, and submission assets.
